answers.core: This would encourage making more secure games, thanks to only having to change one setting once, rather than having to handle a complex dual-synchronizer system or anything else.
answers.workaround:
A way would be to make the server fully authoritative, and expecting player inputs instead of players updating their positions/speed. But this would cause further latency, this is not acceptable for all games.


The following allows disabling `multiplayer.server_relay` and still use synchronizers:

The pawns node could have two synchronizers configured with the same properties.
On the server, one's authority would be the client, the other would be the server.
On the client controlling the pawn, one's authority would be itself, and the other would be disabled.
On other clients, one would be disabled, the other's authority would be set to the server.

Disabling visibility for the client that receive the error on the server-to-client synchronizer have no effect, and the synchronizer keep synchronizing properties (is this a godot bug?). So to disable synchronizers, I set their `delta_time` to an high value to prevent them from sending updates, and I set their authority to a non-existing id to prevent them from considering received updates valid.
